selected_bottleneck: apply-persisted-total-byte-budget-integrity（应用持久化总字节预算完整性）
selected_problem: Fresh canonical main revalidated the per-write MAX_FILE_BYTES limit at apply, but stage also bounded the sum of preimage and postimage bytes for the whole changeset with MAX_TOTAL_BYTES=8,000,000. A durable STAGED document could be coherently expanded into several individually valid writes whose total exceeded 8 MB, and apply would execute all of them.
decision_basis: CHANGESET_TOO_LARGE and MAX_TOTAL_BYTES are existing stage-time transaction resource constraints, so recomputing the same verified-byte total at apply is protocol preservation rather than a new architecture choice.

The defect is directly falsifiable with five unique 1.7 MB self-consistent persisted postimages: each remains below MAX_FILE_BYTES while their 8.5 MB aggregate exceeds the already-approved changeset budget.
Hosted Developer Execution Runtime remained temporarily unavailable with HTTP 502; this cycle used DWAC_SOURCE_CONTRACT_REPLAY（DWAC 源码契约重放） and exact local focused validation.

pre_fix_reality.focused_reproduction: EXPECTED_FAILURE: 1/2 PASS, 1/2 FAIL with Missing expected exception; apply accepted all five 1.7 MB writes and exceeded the 8 MB aggregate stage budget.
pre_fix_reality.impact: Durable reload could increase bounded transaction memory/I/O and side-effect volume beyond what stage had approved even when every individual file remained valid.

change: Apply now sums the actual verified persisted preimage and postimage bytes during preflight and rejects the changeset with CHANGESET_TOO_LARGE as soon as the total exceeds MAX_TOTAL_BYTES, before any workspace mutation.

validation.node_check: PASS on the exact proposed core/changesets.mjs content
validation.focused_tests: 14/14 PASS, 0 skipped across the accumulated apply-integrity regressions
validation.boundary_case: PASS: five 1.6 MB postimages totaling exactly 8,000,000 bytes remain valid and apply

truth_boundary: This preserves the existing aggregate verified-byte budget across durable reload. It is still not an authenticated artifact mechanism and does not protect against a coherent rewrite that remains within all current structural and resource invariants.
